newsitem.title: LEBANON: Police, demonstrators clash in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Police, demonstrators clash in Beirut.

text.p: Lebanese police clashed on Wednesday with demonstrators trying to stage a protest sit-in outside the prime minister's office in Beirut.

Fist fights broke out about 150 metres (yards) from the office of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri when 3,500 demonstrators shouting "Down with Hariri, down with Hariri," tried to break through police barricades.

The demonstrators were protesting against a law slashing the number of private television and radio stations and awarding a handful of licences to stations belonging to prominent establishment figures, including Hariri.
The protesters hit police with sticks from their banners and were clubbed by police rifle butts. A Reuters reporter saw two clashes, one near the prime minister's office and later a few blocks away.
Elias Abu Rizk, head of the General Labour Confederation, one of the main forces behind the protest sit-in, was hit during the second clash.

Hariri, a billionaire who owns one of the four licenced TV and one of the 11 radio stations, has slapped a ban on public demonstrations in Lebanon since 1993 -- the first permanent ban on protests in the country's history.
